verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev workflows are themselves real code: tasks are plain async/await functions with no workflow DSL or determinism rules, written in TypeScript. Steps can be composed via `triggerAndWait()` to pass result data onward, and users confirm they moved from GUI workflows (n8n) to maintaining them in an IDE. missing for 10: no evidence of Python support for steps, and thin documentation of finer-grained step primitives beyond subtask triggering.
